get_free_busy.description: Query busy/free intervals across one or more calendars over a time window
get_free_busy.usage_context: When user wants to check availability, find when someone (or a set of calendars) is busy or free over a period, or lay the groundwork for scheduling. Returns raw busy intervals only (no slot computation). Privacy-safe: surfaces only busy start/end times, never event titles, attendees, or descriptions.

calendar_ids.description: Calendar identifier(s) to query for availability (use 'primary' for the user's primary calendar, or specific calendar IDs/emails). At most 50 calendars per query.

time_min.description: Start of the availability window (RFC3339/ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2026-03-27T00:00:00Z'). Required.

time_max.description: End of the availability window (RFC3339/ISO 8601 format). Required, and must be strictly after time_min.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone used to interpret the response (e.g., 'UTC', 'America/New_York').

max_calendars.message: Cannot query more than 50 calendars in a single free/busy request. Please reduce the number of calendars.

calendars.description: Per-calendar busy intervals. A calendar may carry an 'errors' array (partial success) when it could not be queried (e.g. not found); other calendars still return their busy intervals.

calendar_id.description: The calendar identifier these intervals belong to

busy.description: Busy intervals within the queried window (start/end only — no event details)

errors.description: Per-calendar errors returned by Google for this calendar (e.g. notFound), if any. Present only on partial failure.

time_zone.description: Time zone used to interpret the response (echoed)

queried_at.description: Timestamp when the free/busy query ran (ISO 8601)

list_available_slots.description: Compute open, bookable time slots by subtracting busy intervals from working-hours windows
list_available_slots.usage_context: When user wants to find open times to book/schedule a meeting (a Calendly-style 'here are the times you can book'), given working hours and a slot length. Computes availability deterministically in the executor: queries busy intervals (freebusy) and subtracts them — plus optional buffer padding around meetings and a minimum-notice floor — from the user's working-hours windows, then slices the free time into fixed-length slots. IMPORTANT SEMANTICS: (1) buffer_minutes pads busy blocks on BOTH sides (before/after meetings) — it does NOT add gaps between adjacent free slots, which remain back-to-back. (2) Output slots are UTC 'Z' RFC3339 instants; the working-hours time_zone is echoed for local rendering. (3) This action REPORTS availability only — it books nothing and holds nothing, so a returned slot is not reserved and could be taken by the time an event is created. The search window must not exceed 92 days.

range_start.description: Start of the overall search window (RFC3339/ISO 8601, e.g. '2026-08-01T00:00:00Z'). Required.

range_end.description: End of the overall search window (RFC3339/ISO 8601). Required, must be strictly after range_start, and the window must not exceed 92 days.

slot_duration_minutes.description: Length of each bookable slot in minutes (positive integer, e.g. 30). Required.

working_hours.description: Availability windows plus the IANA time zone that interprets them. time_zone is required (no silent UTC default). Each window lists weekdays + a wall-clock HH:MM start/end in that zone. Multiple windows may share a day to express intra-day breaks (e.g. a lunch break). A weekday not covered by any window is unavailable.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone that interprets every window start/end and day boundary (e.g. 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'). Required.

windows.description: One or more availability rules. Same-day overlapping windows are unioned before slicing.

days.description: Lowercase weekday names this window applies to (e.g. ['monday','tuesday','wednesday','thursday','friday']).

start.description: Wall-clock start time 'HH:MM' (24-hour) in time_zone (e.g. '09:00'). Must be strictly before end.

calendar_ids.description: Calendars whose busy blocks make a slot unavailable (use 'primary' for the user's primary calendar, or specific calendar IDs/emails). At most 50 per query.

buffer_minutes.description: Padding (minutes) applied around EACH busy block on both sides before subtracting — a gap required before and after existing meetings. Does NOT add gaps between adjacent free slots. Must be >= 0.

min_notice_minutes.description: Earliest bookable time relative to now, in minutes (e.g. 120 = no slots within the next 2 hours). Must be >= 0.

max_slots.description: Maximum number of slots to return (chronological, earliest first). Guards against pathological output. Must be >= 0.

max_calendars.message: Cannot query more than 50 calendars in a single availability request. Please reduce the number of calendars.

slots.description: Open, bookable time slots (chronological, earliest first). Each slot is a UTC 'Z' RFC3339 instant pair.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone from working_hours (echoed, for local rendering of the UTC slots)

computed_at.description: Timestamp when the availability was computed (ISO 8601)
